help.consignment-note.note2: When a load is delivered, the shop that posted it is emailed a receipt with a button: Get the consignment note. The button opens the note, every copy of it and its photographs as one file, without signing in, for 30 days. Anybody the email is forwarded to can open it too, so forward it only to somebody who should have the note.
help.consignment-note.note3: The shop sees that link on the note itself. Shop app: “Records › Notes”, then open the note, and look under Links to this note. It shows the address the email went to, how often the file was taken, and until when the link works. Tap Cancel it to stop the link at once. A cancelled link cannot be switched back on.
help.consignment-note.note4: A link hands the file over 25 times at most, and opens nothing once the note itself is no longer kept. The file is the copy to keep: the link stops, the file does not.
help.consignment-note.note5: You can also make a link yourself, for somebody who should have the note and has no account: a bookkeeper, an insurer, the other side. Open the note in your records and, under Links to this note, tap Make a link to pass on. Then tap Send it or Copy it, and send the link in a chat, a text or your own mail. Or open one of its copies — it shows as it will print — and tap Share link there, which hands the link to your phone’s share sheet; in the Shop app, “Consignment note” on the load has the same Share once the note is kept. The link is shown only once, because we keep no copy of it. If it goes astray, cancel it and make another.
help.consignment-note.note6: A note can have five links that work at the same time. Cancel one to make another. Links that no longer work are folded away — tap to show them — with who made each, how often it was opened, and who cancelled it.
help.consignment-note.note8: Riding for yourself, you are the carrier on the note, named with your address: give your business address in the Driver app, or pin the station you work from. A fleet’s driver is never asked — the fleet’s depot is the address.
help.consignment-note.note9: What you note about the goods when you take them over goes on the note. It binds the sender only if the sender agrees; the sender answers once, agreeing or disputing in its own words, and the note says which.
help.consignment-note.note7: A business has no archive: it finds the same file and the same links on the load itself, in the Business app under Domestic › Loads.
help.freight-delivery.title: Deliver a load and record who took it
help.freight-delivery.summary: A load is delivered when somebody took it in. The driver records their name and a photo of the goods as put down; both go on the consignment note. Until the goods are on a truck, the shop can still withdraw the load.
help.freight-delivery.step1: Driver app, at the gate: tick the unload list, type the name of the person who received the goods, take a photo of them where you put them down, and note anything the receiver said. That is box 24 of the consignment note. Count the packages with the receiver against the note’s count. If anything is not as it says, tick “The receiver found something not as the note says” and write only that: packages short, packages more than the note says, packages damaged (with a photo), packages that are not the goods on the note, or packages the receiver refused. It goes on the note beside the receiver’s name, the delivery still stands, and the sender is told.
help.freight-delivery.step2: Driver app, at pickup: if something is already wrong with the goods as handed over — a torn sack, a short count, a wet pallet — write it in the reservations box. The note then shows the goods were like that before you took them over.
help.freight-delivery.step3: Shop app: a delivered load shows who received it and when. Until pickup you can withdraw a load — open it, tap “Withdraw this load” and say why. A driver who had claimed it is told, and a charge you paid comes back. Once it is on a truck, talk to the driver instead.
help.freight-delivery.step4: Driver app, when the goods cannot be handed over: tap “I could not deliver”, say what happened at the door — nobody there, the receiver refused it, or you could not reach the place — and “Record the failed attempt”. The goods stay with you, and the sender is told, so they can ring the receiver or tell you where to take them. Refused, whole or in part: keep the refused goods until the sender says where they go — back, to another place, or given up — within 48 hours; you are told, and you carry them on as a new load the sender pays for. With no answer they go back to where they were picked up, at the sender’s cost. Refused whole and the receiver takes them after all: deliver them as usual.
help.freight-delivery.step5: Shop app, when something is wrong with what arrived: open the load and tap “Report a problem with the goods” within seven days — damaged, short, or not received — with a photo if you have one. A network operator decides it and you are shown their reason. Money can only be awarded where the network billed the load; otherwise the decision says who was right and the carriage is yours and the carrier’s to settle.
help.freight-delivery.note1: Nobody signs on a screen: the driver records the name, and the photo is the proof. A delivered load cannot be withdrawn — a problem with the goods is a claim, not a cancellation.
help.freight-delivery.note2: Only where money is awarded — under cover the company that billed the load has stated — does the carrier bear it: up to what they were paid for the haul and never more. The amount taken back shows on that load in the driver’s and the fleet’s earnings.
help.freight-delivery.note3: A claim on a delivered load — damaged, short, not received — goes onto the consignment note, and the note is frozen with the claim on it: that copy is the damage claim report, under Notes, to hand on by a link. Nobody of the network decides the claim or pays. Only where the company that billed the load has stated cover does a member of staff decide it, up to that cover.
help.freight-delivery.note4: Driver app, a load the shipper pays you for directly: once it has paid you the price agreed, say “I was paid” — on the load, or under Earnings. Delivered and not paid: “Not paid yet” under Earnings, and the shipper is told and sees it on the load. The shipper may answer once that it paid, with a reference you can check — an M-Pesa code, a bank reference — and its answer is shown beside your word. Once the money reaches you, say you were paid. SeeBuyGet carries no money for these loads and judges neither side.
help.sender-instructions.title: Leave instructions for the driver
help.sender-instructions.summary: Every load has a box for what the sender wants the driver to know at the door — the consignment note calls it box 13. A free note, a contact the driver can call, and a delivery window. It goes on the note and to the driver who takes the load.
help.sender-instructions.step1: Shop app, at the counter: when a load is booked as freight — “Book it as freight”, one part at a time, nothing going out before “Book the freight” on its last — take down the contact at delivery and their phone under “Who to call”, and under “On the day” when it should be delivered (“before 10:00”, “second trip”) and anything else the driver needs (“gate on the north side”). All optional.
help.sender-instructions.step2: Shop app, Freight you posted: open the load to read or change the instructions. Until the goods are taken over you can rewrite them. Once the load is on the road you can only add an instruction; it is added with the time, and what the driver was already told stays on the note.
help.sender-instructions.step3: Driver app, My loads: the instructions are on the load card and again at the gate. The phone is a button — tap to call.
help.sender-instructions.step4: Fleet app, Dispatch: the delivery window shows on the load, so the office can choose who to put it on. The contact does not; only the driver holding the load sees a phone number.
help.sender-instructions.step5: Business app: open the load under “Domestic › Loads”, then “On the road”. “At the door” lists each attempt the driver could not hand it over at — when, and why — and under “For the driver”, what the driver is told. “Change the instructions” rewrites them until the goods are taken over; after that, “Add a note for the driver”: the driver who has it is told at once, and what you said before stays.
help.sender-instructions.note1: Instructions are for the door, not for money — the price is agreed on the load itself. The tracking link never shows them, and never the contact’s phone.
help.freight-tracking.title: Track a load and rate the driver
help.freight-tracking.summary: Every load has a tracking link — the same code the consignment note carries as a QR. Whoever holds it sees where the load is, who is carrying it, the day it is expected where it was ordered for one, and who signed for it — and nothing else. After delivery the shop that posted the load rates the driver.
help.freight-tracking.step1: Shop app, Freight you posted: open the load and tap “Tracking link”. Share it, or copy it into a message to whoever is waiting for the goods. They need no account.
help.freight-tracking.step2: Send app, Track: type the code, or open the link. A load climbs its own ladder — waiting for a carrier, booked, on the road, delivered — with the carrier as they will be at the door, any door nobody answered, and who signed.
help.freight-tracking.step3: Shop app, once delivered: tap “Rate the driver”. Stars out of five, and tags for what went wrong if anything. It counts toward the driver’s rating like a shop’s rating at the counter, one verdict per load, and you can change it within 30 days.
help.freight-tracking.note1: The link shows no phone number, no price and no reasons — a withdrawn load says when, never why. What is between the sender and the carrier stays there.
help.freight-tracking.note2: Whoever sent the load is told when it is delivered, with who received it: look under the bell.
help.freight-tracking.note3: A load ordered from a carrier for a day shows that day from the start. Once it is on the road it also shows about when the carrier planned to be at the door. That hour is the carrier’s estimate; it is not shown before the load is on the road, because until then the carrier can still plan the day again. If the hour passes while the load is on the road, or its whole day passes, the page says it is running late instead of going on saying expected.
help.manager-dispatch.title: Put a load on a driver from the office
help.manager-dispatch.summary: A load used to reach a fleet’s driver in two ways only: the driver claimed it, or the network offered it. Now the fleet office can put one on a driver on shift. The office sees the market exactly as that driver would — priced against their vehicle, judged from where they are, every reason it cannot be taken marked — so it can never assign what the driver could not have claimed.
help.manager-dispatch.step1: Fleet app, “Fleet › Dispatch”, or “Find a load” beside a driver on the Shifts tab: choose the driver, choose how far from where they are to look, and read the market for them. What they would earn is their vehicle’s own rate.
help.manager-dispatch.step2: Tap “Put on <name>”. The price is locked at that moment, the load goes on the driver’s list, they are told, and the office’s name is recorded on the load. A load posted for negotiation cannot be assigned — the driver can send the shipper a price from their own board.
help.manager-dispatch.step3: Driver app, My loads: a load the office put on you says so, and by whom. It is collected, carried and delivered exactly like one you claimed, and you are paid the same way.
help.manager-dispatch.note1: A driver has to be on a shift to be given a load, because a load goes on a vehicle and the price is that vehicle’s. What the driver could not take — too heavy, the wrong body, a road that will not carry it — the office cannot force either.
help.fleet-orders.title: Take orders from shippers under contract
help.fleet-orders.summary: A shipper you have a contract with sends its orders straight to you. They are on no board and no other carrier sees them; your office puts each one on a truck.
help.fleet-orders.step1: “Orders › Record a contract”: who you carry for, and the contract number. No price — what you charge them stays on your own contract.
help.fleet-orders.step2: If the shipper has a business on SeeBuyGet, tap Send them a link code and pass the code on. An owner of their business enters it once, and from then on they order with you directly. If they are not, upload their orders yourself as a sheet.
help.fleet-orders.step3: Orders opens on tomorrow: how many orders, how heavy, and how many still have no truck. Choose another day at the top. Anything from an earlier day that has not been delivered stays in sight under Behind.
help.fleet-orders.step4: Open an order to see where it is collected, where it goes and the day it must arrive. While a driver is on a shift you can put it on their truck there and then.
help.fleet-orders.note1: An order is Late when the day it had to arrive has gone by and it has not been delivered. That is read from the order itself, never estimated.
help.fleet-orders.note2: Either side can end a contract. That stops new orders; the ones already placed are still yours to deliver.
help.fleet-order-sheet.title: Upload a sheet of orders
help.fleet-order-sheet.summary: When a shipper sends you its orders as a spreadsheet, upload the sheet under their contract. It is checked line by line before anything is added.
help.fleet-order-sheet.step1: “Orders › Upload orders” beside the contract. Say where the goods are collected: type the place and find it on the map. It is remembered for next time.
help.fleet-order-sheet.step2: Choose the sheet — the Excel workbook itself (.xlsx) or a CSV file — or copy the cells in the spreadsheet and paste them. The first line names the columns: an order number, the goods, the weight, where to deliver and the date. Download a template to send them shows the exact form.
help.fleet-order-sheet.step3: Tap Check the sheet. You see how many orders are ready, how many are already here, and each line with a problem, by its line number and in words.
help.fleet-order-sheet.step4: Tap Add orders. The lines that are right become orders; the others are left out. Put them right and upload the same sheet again — an order number that is already here is never added twice.
help.fleet-order-sheet.step5: An address the map does not know is added without a point and marked in the queue. Open it and place it on the map, or it cannot be planned.
help.fleet-order-sheet.note1: Dates are read as 2026-10-06 or day first, 06/10/2026. Weights may be 4000, 4,000 kg or 1.5 t. A date typed as a date in Excel is read whatever format the cell shows it in.
help.fleet-order-sheet.note2: Your office can withdraw an order it uploaded, with a reason. An order the shipper placed themselves is theirs to withdraw.
help.fleet-order-sheet.note4: For the consignment note, a sheet may also have a Consignee column (who receives each order at its address), the dangerous goods’ UN number, class, proper shipping name and packing group, and Customs instructions. Each is read only where the sheet has the column; a line whose dangerous goods are named only in part says what is missing and is not imported.
help.fleet-order-sheet.note3: Of an Excel workbook the first sheet is read, and you are told its name and which sheets were not read. Problems are reported by the line numbers Excel shows. An old .xls file and a workbook with a password are not read: save it as .xlsx or as CSV. A workbook over 1 MB is refused before it is sent, with its size: keep only the sheet with the orders on it, or copy the cells and paste them.
help.fleet-plan.title: Plan which truck takes which orders
help.fleet-plan.summary: The app works out a plan for a day’s orders on your own trucks, and tells you how many trucks short you are. Best read on a laptop.
help.fleet-plan.step1: Orders, choose the day, then Plan this day. The first line is the answer: how many of the day’s orders are on a truck, and how many more trucks you would need for the rest.
help.fleet-plan.step2: Under it, what does not fit, grouped by why: an address not on the map (pin it and plan again), no room left in the day, a free truck with no driver, goods no truck of yours can handle, or an order heavier than your largest truck (split it into loads).
help.fleet-plan.step3: An order heavier than your largest truck has Split it into loads. The plan says how many loads of your largest vehicle it makes; you can choose more. Each load then is an order of its own — planned, put on a truck, signed for and tracked separately — and the shipper is told its order comes in parts. Open any load and tap Put the order back together to undo it, while no load is on a truck or handed on.
help.fleet-plan.step4: Then each truck’s day, trip after trip in the order it is driven. A truck that has unloaded goes on to its next collection from where it is, not from the depot.
help.fleet-plan.step5: Where a shipper asked for a delivery window, the plan goes for it: a vehicle that is early waits for the window to open, and the door that closes soonest is visited first. An order that cannot make its window is planned all the same and marked with how late it will be — or how early, when the day has no room to wait. The first lines of the plan say how many.
help.fleet-plan.step6: Change the day opens your settings: when trucks leave, the longest day, the speed on the road, the minutes to load and to hand over, and which vehicles go out. Change one and the plan is worked out again.
help.fleet-plan.step7: Accept this plan when it is right. Each order then shows its truck, its trip and about when it arrives. Opening the plan later shows it as accepted; Plan the day again works out a new one, which replaces it only when you accept that.
help.fleet-plan.step8: On the day itself the plan goes out by itself, a trip at a time: a truck gets its first trip when its driver starts a shift in it, and the next when the last order of that trip is delivered. Send the next trips out now does the same by hand, and says what each truck is doing.
help.fleet-plan.note1: Every time on the plan is an estimate: distance at one speed, plus fixed minutes at each stop — so is “late” and “early”. Distances are by road where the service has a routing server, and an estimate — straight lines with an allowance for the road — where it has not, or when it cannot be reached. The plan says which, under its first lines.
help.fleet-plan.note2: A truck is only ever given one trip at a time — what it can carry at once. Every order goes on with the same checks as any load (room, equipment, the driver’s hours). One that is refused stays in the queue with the reason on it.
help.fleet-plan.note3: The plan never loads a truck past what it carries, never makes a day longer than you set (13 hours at most), and sends out no more vehicles than you have drivers.
help.fleet-plan.note4: The plan will leave one order out when that lets it deliver more of the others: a far, heavy load can hold a truck that three nearer orders would fill. It never gives one order up for one. What is left out is listed with its reason and counted in the trucks you are short.
help.fleet-plan.note5: A window is read when it is written as hours: 8-12, 08:00-12:00, before 14:00, after 9, 2pm-5pm. Words such as morning, or hours that could be either half of the day (1-5), are not read: the order is planned to its day only and says so. Nothing is ever left out because of a window.
help.fleet-plan.note6: Accepting a plan tells shippers two things, and the plan says so above the Accept button when either applies. The shipper of an order the plan leaves out is told it is on no vehicle and why: no room that day, no vehicle that can carry it, heavier than your largest vehicle, or no point on the map. They are never told anything about your drivers. The shipper of an order planned outside its window is told about when, and by how much.
help.fleet-plan.note7: Accepting the same day again repeats nothing. A shipper hears again only when something changed: another reason for being left out, a time that moved by half an hour or more, or an order that is on a vehicle after all. A shipper also sees, in its own app, about when each of its planned orders arrives. Whoever holds an order’s tracking link sees its day, and about when once the load is on the road. An order your own office typed in or uploaded has nobody to tell.
help.fleet-plan.note8: Every time on a plan is on your office’s own clock, and the plan says which under its first lines. You do not set it: a fleet keeps the time zone of its country. Only where a country keeps more than one does the board ask you to choose, once. “Today” is today on that clock, so a shift that starts just after midnight gets that day’s trips.
help.fleet-plan.note9: With a clock, shippers can be told two more things, and are. When a load is handed over, its shipper is told the time and whether that was inside the window they asked for. When a load has not arrived half an hour after the time your plan gave, its shipper is told it is running late, and told once more if the whole day passes.
help.fleet-plan.note10: A shipper is also told when an order for today is on no vehicle at seven in the morning on your clock, or an hour after it was ordered if that is later. That is a day with no accepted plan, an order placed after the plan, or an order that missed its trip. Nobody is told during the night. They are told again when it is on a vehicle: when you accept a plan with it in, or put it on a driver by hand.
help.fleet-plan-adviser.title: Ask about a plan and say what to change
help.fleet-plan-adviser.summary: On a plan you have not accepted yet you can ask an AI adviser why the plan is the way it is, or tell it in your own words what should be different. It explains, and it asks the planner again. The planner still does the planning.
help.fleet-plan-adviser.step1: Orders, choose the day, then Plan this day. Under the answer is Ask about this plan. Type a question — why is this order left out, why is that truck not going out — and tap Ask.
help.fleet-plan-adviser.step2: Or say what to change: keep FRT-142 off KLM 808T, start at six, the small truck is in the workshop, allow eleven hours. The adviser changes what the planner is asked, the plan is worked out again, and the board shows the new one.
help.fleet-plan-adviser.step3: Under each answer the app says what was changed, or that nothing was. That line comes from the planner, not from the adviser: if the two ever disagree, believe that line and the plan on the board.
help.fleet-plan-adviser.step4: A rule you asked for stays on the board under Rules on this plan: an order kept off a vehicle, or an order put on one vehicle and no other. It holds every time the day is planned again. Tap Remove to take it off.
help.fleet-plan-adviser.step5: Without the adviser: open Change the day. Under each stop, Not on this vehicle keeps that order off that vehicle and Move to puts it on another. An order the plan left out has Put on.
help.fleet-plan-adviser.step6: Nothing is accepted by asking. When the plan is right, Accept this plan is still yours to tap. The rules a plan was accepted under are kept with it.
help.fleet-plan-adviser.note1: The adviser can change when vehicles leave, the longest day, the speed on the road, the minutes to load and to hand over, which vehicles go out, and rules about one order and one vehicle. It cannot change a delivery window or the order of stops, or split an order; it says so when asked. It can tell you which orders are planned late for their window and why.
help.fleet-plan-adviser.note2: It cannot break the plan’s own limits: no vehicle loaded past what it carries, no day over 13 hours, no more vehicles out than you have drivers. An order put on a vehicle too small for it is left out, and the board says a rule is why.
help.fleet-plan-adviser.note3: What goes to the AI service to answer you: your words, and the plan — order codes, shippers’ names, delivery addresses, weights and plates. No phone numbers and no contact names.
help.fleet-plan-adviser.note4: If the adviser is not switched on, is busy or cannot be reached, the plan is unaffected. Change the day still does the settings and the vehicles by hand.
help.fleet-plan-adviser.note5: It is an AI and can misread a question. It never writes the plan itself, so a wrong answer cannot put an order on a truck.
help.fleet-partners.title: Offer orders to partners or the open board
help.fleet-partners.summary: Orders your own trucks cannot take go to the fleets you work with first. What no partner takes can go on the open board.
help.fleet-partners.step1: “Orders › Partners”. Name a fleet you hand work to and you are shown a code once. Send it to their office; they enter it under their own Partners. From then on you can offer them orders. Either of you can end it.
help.fleet-partners.step2: To offer one order, open it and tap Offer it to your partners. To offer everything a plan left out, tap Offer them to your partners on the plan. All your partners are asked at once; the first to take an order carries it.
help.fleet-partners.step3: A partner sees what it needs to decide: what, from where to where, how heavy, for which day. It does not see whose customer it is until it takes the order.
help.fleet-partners.step4: An order on offer is not in your own plan and cannot go on your own trucks. Take the offer back to carry it yourself.
help.fleet-partners.step5: What no partner takes: open the order and tap Put it on the open board. Any checked carrier can take it at the board’s price, and you pay them yourself. Take it back off the board while nobody has it.
help.fleet-partners.step6: Orders a partner offers YOU are at the top of Orders. Take one and it is yours to plan and carry; leave it and it goes to their other partners. If you took one and cannot carry it after all, give it back with a reason — until it is on one of your trucks.
help.fleet-partners.step7: Passing on. Under Partners, tick They may pass my orders on beside a partner you trust to. That partner can then offer an order it took from you to its own partners; the first to take it carries it, and the order shows you who. Untick it and their open offers are taken back. An order somebody is already carrying stays with them.
help.fleet-partners.step8: If a fleet has ticked that for you, an order you took from it has Pass it on to your partners. It can be passed on once: the fleet that takes it carries it or gives it back to you, and you can still give it back to the fleet it came from.
help.fleet-partners.note1: You stay the carrier your shipper ordered from. The consignment note names whoever actually carried the goods.
help.fleet-partners.note2: You are told when a partner takes an order, when no partner took it, and when one gives it back and why. A partner is told when you offer and when you take an offer back.
help.fleet-partners.note3: The price between you and a partner, or a carrier from the board, is yours to agree and pay. SeeBuyGet does not handle it.
help.fleet-partners.note4: A fleet being offered an order that is passed on sees which fleet is offering it — not the fleet it was first ordered from, nor whose customer it is, until it takes it. The consignment note names whoever carried.
help.papers-that-expire.title: Renew insurance, inspection or a licence
help.papers-that-expire.summary: A vehicle’s insurance and inspection certificate and a driver’s licence each carry an expiry date. The day after that date passes, the vehicle or driver is off the road until the renewal is recorded — by the fleet office, or for a courier without a fleet, by network staff. A driver sends a photo of the renewed card from the Driver app to whichever of the two records their licence. A paper with no date recorded switches nothing off — and nothing watches it for you either.
help.papers-that-expire.step1: Fleet app, Vehicles: record the policy number and the expiry date when you register a vehicle, or later with “Papers” under the vehicle. The same sheet is where you record a renewal — the new date is the whole of it.
help.papers-that-expire.step2: Fleet app, Drivers: a driver whose licence is running out sends a photo of the new card from their own app, and it arrives here. The Drivers tab shows how many are waiting, and those drivers come first with “Read the card”. Open it and the photo is shown at a readable size, with the date they read beside the field: type the date you read yourself — one that differs from theirs is pointed out before it is saved — or choose “Not accepted” and say why, in a sentence the driver is shown. With no card sent, “Licence” under a driver records the date from the card as you have seen it, as before. Only the fleet office can record it; the driver’s own word about their own licence is what the date is there to replace.
help.papers-that-expire.step3: Fleet app, Fleet: the Papers card lists what has lapsed and what runs out within 30 days, soonest first, and says how many papers are in date and how many have no date at all.
help.papers-that-expire.step4: Every six hours the network checks every fleet. A vehicle or driver already on a shift when a paper lapses has the shift ended and the driver told why, and the fleet’s contact address is emailed what is off the road and what is running out — once per paper, so a renewed paper starts a new clock and an ignored email is never repeated.
help.papers-that-expire.step5: Driver app: a licence running out is said on the start screen ahead of the day it stops you, with a button to send a photo of the renewed card and the date you read off it. In a fleet, it goes to your own fleet office, and you can still show them the card instead. Sending it changes nothing yet — your office reads the same photo and records the date, or tells you why it could not, and you are told either way. A vehicle off the road is listed, marked, and refused at the scan with the paper named, so you know what to ask the office for.
